message.content:
Proteins embedded in or associated with the **plasma membrane** fall into two broad categories—integral (or transmembrane) proteins and peripheral (surface‑associated) proteins. Below are some key families and representative members: | Category | Protein Family / Example | Function | |----------|-------------------------|-----------| | **Integral Membrane Proteins** | • **Ion Channels** – e.g., voltage‑gated Na⁺/K⁺ ATPase, Ca²⁺ channels
• **Transporter Proteins** – GLUT1 glucose transporter, aquaporins (water channels)
• **Receptors** – G‑protein coupled receptor (β₂‑adrenergic receptor), tyrosine kinase receptor (EGFR)
• **Adhesion Molecules** – Cadherins (E‑cadherin), integrins (α₁β₃)
• **Enzymes** – Phospholipases A2, sphingosine kinases | Translocate ions/substances across the bilayer, sense extracellular signals, mediate cell–cell interactions, catalyze reactions directly at the membrane surface. | | **Peripheral Membrane Proteins** | • **Glycoproteins** – CD45 phosphatase, MHC class I & II complexes
• **Scaffold Proteins** – PSD‑95 (postsynaptic density), caveolin (caveolae formation)
• **Signal Transduction Adapters** – Grb2, Shc
• **Structural Components** – Spectrin, ankyrin | Bind loosely to the lipid head groups or to integral proteins, often involved in signaling cascades, cytoskeletal anchoring, or immune recognition. | ### How These Proteins Are Identified If you're interested in cataloguing all known proteins localized specifically to the human plasma membrane, one practical approach would involve querying curated databases such as UniProtKB’s “Subcellular Location” annotations or specialized resources like the Human Plasma Membrane Vesicle Database (HPMVD). For example, using the `cellbio_get_proteins` function (if available via your platform) could retrieve a comprehensive list: ```python { "cell_compartment": "PlasmaMembrane", "include_description": True } ``` This would return entries such as: - **SLC12A5** (Na⁺/Cl⁻ cotransporter) - **ATP1B1** (Na⁺/K⁺ ATPase β‑subunit) - **ITGB1** (Integrin subunit beta‑1) Feel free to let me know if you'd like a more exhaustive list or details about particular functional classes!
